chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I saw Mismāʿ in al-Madinah, and he had carried wealth to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that year, but Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام returned it. So I said to him, “Why did Abū ʿAbdillāh return to you the wealth that you carried to him?” He said: He said to me, “I said to him when I carried the wealth to him: I had been appointed over pearl-diving in al-Baḥrayn, and I obtained four hundred thousand dirhams. I have come to you with its khums, eighty thousand dirhams, and I disliked withholding it from you or exposing it [to loss], while it is your right which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has placed in our wealth.”

So he said: “Is there for us, from the land and what Allah brings forth from it, only the khums? O Abū Sayyār, surely all the earth belongs to us, so whatever Allah brings forth from it of anything, it is ours.” I said to him, “Then I should carry all of the wealth to you?” He said: “O Abū Sayyār, we have made it wholesome for you and permitted you regarding it. So keep your wealth with you. And everything of the land that is in the hands of our Shiʿah is lawful for them until our Qāʾim rises.”

Then he will collect from them the levy of what was in their hands, and he will leave the land in their hands. But as for what is in the hands of others, their earnings from the land are haram for them until our Qāʾim rises, whereupon he will take the land from their hands and expel them in humiliation.

ʿUmar ibn Yazid said: Then Abū Sayyār said to me, “I do not regard anyone among the owners of estates, nor those who administer official functions, as consuming what is halal besides me, except one for whom they have made that lawful.”

key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the land or earth, described here as belonging entirely to them
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth due mentioned here in relation to wealth and rights
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: forbidden or unlawful, describing the earnings of others from the land
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shiʿah, those granted permissibility regarding land in their possession
key_terms.طَيَّبْنَاهُ: we have made it wholesome or lawful for you
key_terms.قَائِمُنَا: our Qāʾim, whose rise is linked to future enforcement
key_terms.مُحَلَّلُونَ: rendered lawful or permitted with respect to that possession

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in al-Kafi say about khums, ownership of the earth, and the Shiʿah’s use of land until the rise of the Qāʾim عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imam عليه السلام declared the earth and what it produces to belong to them, and that he permitted his Shiʿah to benefit from what is in their possession until the قيام of the Qāʾim عليه السلام. It also presents a ruling concerning permissibility, khums, and the differing status of land held by the Shiʿah and others.
